html:
Bigo bya Mugenyi is a large complex of ditches and earthworks in western Uganda, near the Katonga river, dug around the 14th and 15th centuries.

The ditches, several kilometres long and in places several metres deep, enclosed cattle and a central area. They suggest a powerful state of cattle keepers, which oral tradition remembers as Kitara, ruled by the Chwezi, semi-divine kings who are said to have vanished.

The kingdoms of Bunyoro, Ankole and later Buganda claimed descent from or succession to that world, and spirits of the Chwezi were honoured in their religion. It is the main early site of the great lakes kingdoms of Uganda.
sum: Bigo bya Mugenyi is a large complex of ditches and earthworks in western Uganda, near the Katonga river, dug around the 14th and 15th centuries.
